summary: Milestone 2026.08.532 completed 3 experiments in 4.2 minutes. The only compute-bound experiment was the shortest recorded entry, while the 2 synthesis-only tasks formed the runtime tail; the task-scoped GPU-idle classification is false.
bottlenecks_identified: The 2.85-minute dated evidence refresh was the longest recorded path; as synthesis-only work, it is a workflow-latency target rather than a GPU bottleneck.
The 1.3-minute terminal-boundary handoff was the other material contributor to the visible runtime tail.
Disk-mtime reconstruction and a single GPU snapshot do not provide phase-level causes or task-lifetime utilization attribution.
improvements_suggested: Add incremental, content-addressed caching to the dated evidence refresh so unchanged evidence can reuse a validated prior scan.
Generate terminal-boundary handoff receipts from the prior milestone's validated manifest instead of rebuilding unchanged handoff state.
Record task-scoped start and stop timestamps with GPU utilization samples for compute-bound work so utilization is attributable to the task lifetime.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Cache and incrementally refresh dated evidence.
Automate terminal-boundary handoff generation from validated manifests.
Capture task-scoped phase timing and GPU telemetry for compute-bound work.
meta_reflection: The sole compute-bound entry is the longest compute-bound experiment by default and completed in 0.01 minutes, but no data is available this milestone to explain why it took that long. Its task-scoped GPU-idle flag is false, and no data is available this milestone for a compute-bound task loading multiple models in parallel, so no DualGPURunner miss is established; the upper-bound savings estimate is the rounded share of wall time occupied by the longest synthesis workflow.
